credit: Retold in our own words from Ascension’s The Bible in a Year podcast with Fr. Mike Schmitz (built on Jeff Cavins’ Great Adventure Bible Timeline), with notes from the Catechism of the Catholic Church, the Church Fathers (New Advent), and Haydock’s Catholic Bible Commentary (1859). Not affiliated with Ascension.

2026-10-24.title: Using Good Things for Evil
2026-10-24.period: Maccabean Revolt, read alongside the Wisdom books
2026-10-24.reflection: Today 1 Maccabees comes to its end. Simon, the last of Mattathias’ sons, is murdered at a banquet by his own son-in-law, a man with plenty of silver and gold whose heart was lifted up. Fr. Mike pairs that with Sirach and Proverbs: everything God made is good, wine, medicine, skill, wealth, but we can turn good things toward evil ends. Sirach tells us to honor the physician and to pray, because healing comes from the Most High. Proverbs paints the person who lingers over wine with red eyes and a sore heart. The gift is not the problem. The question is what we do with it.

ccc.text: Temperance asks us to avoid every kind of excess: food, alcohol, tobacco, or medicine. Endangering our own or others’ safety through drunkenness is a grave fault.

father.work: On the Care to Be Had for the Dead
father.text: On Sirach’s call to bury the dead with care, Augustine says funerals, burial and its honors are more a comfort for the living than a help to the dead. What helps the dead is prayer, alms and the Mass offered for them.

haydock.text: We should neither trust doctors too much nor despise them. Despising them would be tempting God.

2026-10-24.question: Which good gift in my life am I tempted to use for something God never meant it for?

2026-10-25.title: The Gift of Life
2026-10-25.period: Maccabean Revolt, read alongside the Wisdom books
2026-10-25.confirmed: 2025 episode page (the 2026 replay was not posted yet)
2026-10-25.reflection: 2 Maccabees opens with letters to the Jews in Egypt, inviting them to keep the feast of the Temple’s purification. Fr. Mike sets the scene: this book retells some of 1 Maccabees from a more God-centered angle. He tells the story of the sacred fire hidden before the exile and found by Nehemiah as a thick liquid that burst into flame on the altar. Sirach 41 then speaks of death, bitter to the comfortable and welcome to the worn out. Fr. Mike speaks gently to anyone grieving: our lives, and the lives of those we love, are a gift.

ccc.text: Death ends our earthly life. Remembering that our time is limited reminds us that we have only a set span in which to live out our lives.

father.work: On the Death of Satyrus, Book I
father.text: Ambrose preached at his own brother’s funeral. He admits his grief openly, then lets St. Paul’s words about not grieving like those without hope rein in his sorrow.

haydock.text: Nehemiah has the priests sprinkle the thick water over the wood and the sacrifice. Haydock compares it to Elijah calling down fire on his sacrifice.

2026-10-25.question: Whose life am I thanking God for today, even if I miss them?

2026-10-26.title: Jeremiah Hides the Ark
2026-10-26.period: Maccabean Revolt, read alongside the Wisdom books
2026-10-26.confirmed: 2025 episode page (the 2026 replay was not posted yet)
2026-10-26.reflection: Jeremiah, warned by God, takes the tent, the Ark and the altar of incense to the mountain where Moses saw the promised land. He seals them in a cave whose place is to stay unknown until God gathers his people again. Fr. Mike explains where the Ark was hidden and what its absence meant for God’s people. He looks ahead to the rest of 2 Maccabees. Then Sirach 44 begins its praise of famous men, which leads to his question for us: what will the people who love us remember about us?

ccc.text: Mary is the one in whom the Lord himself has just made his dwelling. She is the daughter of Zion in person, the ark of the covenant, the place where the glory of the Lord dwells.

father.work: On the Duties of the Clergy, Book III
father.text: Ambrose retells how the priests hid the altar fire before the exile, and how it returned as water and then fire. He reads it as a sign of grace, which burns away sin like fire and washes it away like water.

haydock.text: The Ark most likely never stood in the second Temple. The promise points to the Messiah, whom the Ark prefigured. God was drawing his people from visible signs toward spiritual realities.

2026-10-26.question: What do I hope the people who love me will remember about how I loved God?

2026-10-27.title: Conversion of Heart
2026-10-27.period: Maccabean Revolt, read alongside the Wisdom books
2026-10-27.confirmed: 2025 episode page (the 2026 replay was not posted yet)
2026-10-27.reflection: Heliodorus comes to rob the Temple treasury. A rider in golden armor and two strong young men drive him back, and he is spared only by the high priest’s prayer. Fr. Mike contrasts the two books: 1 Maccabees tells events from a more secular angle, while 2 Maccabees keeps pointing to God at work. He asks us to look at our own days the same way, seeing God in each moment of our story. He also tells the conversion of St. Mary of Egypt, whose heart changed completely.

ccc.text: Jesus’ call to conversion and penance aims first at the heart, at interior conversion, not at outward works like sackcloth and ashes.

father.text: Augustine describes how long his will stayed divided, wanting God but saying “not yet.” In a garden in Milan, he hears a voice say “take up and read,” opens St. Paul, and his heart is finally turned.

haydock.text: The heavenly horse and rider are compared to the fiery horses that took Elijah and filled the mountain around Elisha. Haydock points to St. Ambrose for more on this story.

2026-10-27.question: Where did God show up in my day today that I almost missed?

2026-10-28.title: Rising Again
2026-10-28.period: Maccabean Revolt, read alongside the Wisdom books
2026-10-28.confirmed: 2025 episode page (the 2026 replay was not posted yet)
2026-10-28.reflection: Jason buys the high priesthood and brings Greek ways into Jerusalem, and Menelaus outbids him. Meanwhile Sirach walks back through the whole story we have read this year: David, Solomon, Elijah, Elisha, Hezekiah, Josiah. As the Old Testament winds down, Fr. Mike points out that Scripture keeps saying one thing. Get back up after sin and return to God, because he always lifts us again with his mercy. “The just man falls seven times and rises.”

ccc.text: The Gospel reveals, in Jesus Christ, God’s mercy to sinners.

father.text: Chrysostom writes to a friend who has given up his vows. He says the devil’s aim in pushing us toward despair is to cut the anchor of our hope in God. Repentance is never closed to us.

haydock.text: The just person still has many failings and venial sins and does not lose the name of just. The wicked person who consents to mortal sin does not rise again so easily.

2026-10-28.question: What fall am I still lying in, and what would rising look like this week?

2026-10-29.title: The Pursuit of Wisdom
2026-10-29.period: Maccabean Revolt, read alongside the Wisdom books
2026-10-29.confirmed: 2025 episode page (the 2026 replay was not posted yet)
2026-10-29.reflection: Sirach ends with the high priest Simon shining in the Temple and with Ben Sira’s prayer of thanks and his invitation to seek wisdom. Fr. Mike encourages us to keep pursuing it. In 2 Maccabees, the Temple is plundered again, and Judas Maccabeus slips away into the hills to live clean among the wild beasts. Proverbs adds a hard word: do not rejoice when your enemy falls.

ccc.text: Deliberate hatred is contrary to charity. Wanting evil for our neighbor is a grave sin. Christ asks us to love our enemies and pray for those who persecute us.

father.text: Preaching on “love your enemies,” Chrysostom calls this the highest peak of virtue. It is not enough to bear a wrong. We are to pray for and do good to the one who did it.

haydock.text: If we gloat, God may turn his anger away from our enemy, and our thirst for revenge comes to nothing.

2026-10-29.question: Whose fall have I secretly enjoyed, and can I pray for them by name tonight?

2026-10-30.title: Eleazar's Martyrdom
2026-10-30.period: Maccabean Revolt, read alongside the Wisdom books
2026-10-30.confirmed: 2025 episode page (the 2026 replay was not posted yet)
2026-10-30.reflection: Eleazar, ninety years old, refuses to eat pork, and he refuses even to pretend to, though friends offer him a way out. Fr. Mike marvels at his courage: he avoids sin, and he refuses to lead the young into sin by his example. Then we open the Book of Wisdom. Three lessons: God did not make death, death entered the world through sin, and we are wise when we walk in truth and foolish when we walk in evil.

ccc.text: “God did not make death, and he does not delight in the death of the living… It was through the devil’s envy that death entered the world” (Wis 1:13; 2:24).

father.work: On Jacob, quoted by Haydock on 2 Maccabees 6:24
father.text: Ambrose says old age should be the harbor of a life well lived, not its shipwreck. Eleazar lives it out: he will not shame his gray hair at the very end.

haydock.text: The pity Eleazar’s friends show is called wicked, because it suggested saving his life by pretending. Faking consent to a false religion is never lawful.

2026-10-30.question: Who is watching my example, and what is it teaching them?

2026-10-31.title: Life Beyond Death
2026-10-31.period: Maccabean Revolt, read alongside the Wisdom books
2026-10-31.confirmed: 2025 episode page (the 2026 replay was not posted yet)
2026-10-31.reflection: Seven brothers and their mother refuse to break God’s law, one after another, and they hold fast to the hope of the resurrection. Fr. Mike says one theme ties all of today’s readings together: life beyond death. Wisdom 3 says the souls of the just are in the hand of God and no torment will touch them. Death is not the end. Eternal life is waiting.

ccc.text: God revealed the resurrection of the dead to his people step by step. The martyrdom of the seven brothers in 2 Maccabees shows that hope: the King of the universe will raise us up to everlasting life.

father.who: St. Gregory of Nazianzus and other Fathers, as noted by Haydock on 2 Maccabees 7:41
father.text: The Church honored these martyrs from the earliest centuries, before any other saints of the Old Testament. Gregory, Maximus of Turin and Gaudentius preached their praises. Haydock calls them the martyrs of the resurrection.

haydock.text: The resurrection is stated plainly in each brother’s answer, and the Redeemer was near at hand.

2026-10-31.question: What would change in how I live this week if I really believed the resurrection?

2026-11-01.title: The Defender
2026-11-01.period: Maccabean Revolt, read alongside the Wisdom books
2026-11-01.confirmed: 2025 episode page (the 2026 replay was not posted yet)
2026-11-01.reflection: 2 Maccabees tells again how Judas Maccabeus and his brothers fought for the honor of the Temple, but this time we see how clearly they knew God was present, merciful and just in what they faced. Fr. Mike’s point is simple: whatever we are going through, God is our great defender, present and at work in every part of our lives. Wisdom 5 shows the just standing with great confidence before those who mocked them, and on All Saints’ Day that is a fitting picture of the saints.

ccc.text: The saints in heaven, being more closely united to Christ, do not stop interceding for us with the Father. Their brotherly care is a great help to our weakness.

father.who: St. Augustine, as noted by Haydock on Wisdom 5:17
father.work: Sermon on the life of the apostles
father.text: Scripture pictures the glory of the saints as a crown, and the joy of the elect is to lay those crowns before God’s throne, because in him they find everything good.

haydock.text: Worldly people laugh at those who work for the goods of eternity and think they labor in vain. At the judgment, the just stand firm.

2026-11-01.question: Which saint do I want standing beside me as a defender this month, and what will I ask them?
